item.title: The Four-Model Scott Complexity Spectrum: $F(4)=8$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gonzalez, Rossegger, and Turetsky introduced a spectrum-counting function $F(n)$ for the Scott complexities realized by $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_2$ theories with exactly $n$ countable models. They proved $7\leq F(4)\leq 8$ and left the exact value open. We prove $F(4)=8$. More precisely, we construct a $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_2$ sentence with exactly four countable models whose optimal Scott complexities are $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_2$, $\Sigma^{\mathrm{in}}_3$, $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_3$, and $d\text{-}\Sigma^{\mathrm{in}}_3$, one of each. The construction starts with a complete first-order Ehrenfeucht theory having exactly two almost-prime and two limit models, whose existence follows from a realization theorem of Sudoplatov, and then passes to a full first-order Morleyization. The proof is organized around two low-level transfer principles. First, in a small theory, a $\Sigma^{\mathrm{in}}_3$ Scott sentence forces a model to be prime over a finite tuple; after Morleyization the converse holds. Second, if a model realizes every complete finite-tuple type over the empty set, then every $\Pi^{\mathrm{in}}_3$ sentence true in it is true in the countable saturated model. These two principles force the four models into the four distinct Scott-complexity classes above.
item.dc:creator: Yueer Yang

item.title: Universally Measurable Sets and Correlated Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2611.13335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study alternate definitions of correlated equilibrium in games with Polish strategy spaces. We first consider universally measurable decision problems equipped with a measure assignment and a prior, comparing deviation stability with the stronger requirement of conditional rationality. We show they are equivalent for Borel measurable problems, but their equivalence for all analytically measurable problems depends on the model of set theory. The full equivalence follows from $\mathsf{MUP}$, while a nonmeasurable set of reals yields a counterexample. When the set of strategies which are best responses to their assigned measures is measurable by the prior, we characterize the equivalence by the principle $\mathsf{MUP}^{\mathsf{UM}}$, which holds in a model of Larson--Neeman--Shelah. The results carry over to games, where we further show that conditionally rational priors must concentrate on $\text{RCBR}$ strategies, while deviation stable priors may fail to do so even in games with analytically measurable payoffs. This provides an epistemic justification for defining a correlated equilibrium as a conditionally rational prior.
item.dc:creator: Stuart Zoble

item.title: The unavoidable minor in graphs of uncountable edge-connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.13390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any given uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, we show that every $\kappa$-edge-connected graph admits a minor embedding of the graph $T_{\kappa}\star1$ (the $\kappa$-regular tree with a new apex vertex adjacent to all its nodes), which is itself $\kappa$-edge-connected. This extends a previous result of Kurkofka regarding unavoidable minors of $\aleph_0$-edge-connected graphs to all uncountable cardinalities $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Max Pitz, Lucas Real, Roman Schaut

item.title: G\"odel's Incompleteness Theorems in Grounded Arithmetic
item.description: arXiv:2611.13697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) is a paracomplete arithmetic in which every term is a program and truth is grounded evaluation. RGA discharges a hypothesis only when it proves the hypothesis decided. This paper shows, in a machine-checked Isabelle/HOL development, how G\"odel's incompleteness theorems hold for RGA and for systems built on it. RGA's implication is material and RGA has the disjunction property, so the implications the textbook proof of the second theorem uses fail while its entailments and rules hold: G\"odel's proof survives as entailments. RGA does not prove its consistency sentence Con, and RGA derives its own second theorem as the entailment $\mathit{Con}\vdash\neg\mathit{Pr}(\ulcorner\mathit{Con}\urcorner)$ and as one sentence quantified over proofs. The second theorem is then proved once, for every G\"odel extension of RGA: an entailment relation on RGA's language, closed under RGA's rules, with a checker that meets three structural conditions, NEC, D3 and EXPL as proof transformers, D1 as closed acceptance, and consistency. D2 is not among the conditions. RGA with its checker is one instance. Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA), RGA with ground induction, is another, its checker adding one rule detector, and IGA does not derive its consistency sentence for it. Adoption, a reflection rule whose premise is a derived warrant that the checker accepts computed proofs of every instance of a universal, gives consistent extensions RGA$^+$ and IGA$^+$. RGA$^+$ derives RGA's consistency sentence and IGA$^+$ derives RGA's and IGA's, so each strictly extends its base, and IGA$^+$ both. The second theorem holds at every adopted notation claim, and adopting Turing's code for that claim's checker derives its consistency sentence, so no claim certifies itself. Whether IGA alone derives RGA's consistency sentence is open, and the paper names what two routes to an answer need.
item.dc:creator: Bryan Ford

item.title: Independent Families Under Determinacy-Like Hypotheses
item.description: arXiv:2611.14366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize the notion of an independent family on $\omega$ to $\mathcal{J}$-independent families on an arbitrary cardinal $\kappa$ and then show that under determinacy-like hypotheses that there can be no such families for reasonable $\mathcal{J}$. This is quite atypical as all other generalizations of the kinds of combinatorial families coming from the theory of cardinal characteristics follow a very different pattern, which will also be explained; in this sense independent families seem particularly special. The base theory assumed throughout is $\textsf{ZF + }$All infinite sets are Dedekind infinite.
item.dc:creator: Stewart Bahrke, Nam Trang

item.title: Topology idealized
item.description: arXiv:2611.13706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by recent work of A. Njamcul and A. Pavlovi\'c, we study topological spaces expanded by ideals of sets. We investigate the relationship between the cardinal invariants of the ideal topological space $(X, \tau_\mathcal{I})$, the underlying topology $(X, \tau)$, and the cardinal characteristics of the ideal $\mathcal{I}$. Furthermore, we analyze continuous maps between standard Polish spaces and their ideal expansions. We establish rigidity phenomena showing that continuous functions from $(X, \tau)$ into $(X, \tau_\mathcal{I})$ are severely constrained (e.g., taking at most countably many values on Polish spaces and being strictly constant on $\mathbb{R}$), whereas continuous functions from $(\mathbb{R}, \tau_\mathcal{I})$ to $(\mathbb{R}, \tau)$ collapse to standard continuous functions under mild conditions on the ideal.
item.dc:creator: Grzegorz We{\l}yczko, Szymon \.Zeberski

item.title: Automatic Continuity for projective clone homomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.14490v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that every projective clone homomorphism from a closed function clone containing the automorphism group of a countable homogeneous Ramsey structure $\Delta$ in a finite relational language is uniformly continuous. This answers, for such structures, open questions previously raised by Barto, Bodirsky, Marimon, Pongr\'acz, and the second author in several papers (Bodirsky, Pinsker, Pongr\'acz, J. Symb. Log. 2021; Barto, Pinsker, SIAM J. Comput. 2020; Marimon, Pinsker, arXiv:2512.01086). Consequently, the polymorphism clone of a first-order reduct $\Gamma$ of $\Delta$ admits a projective clone homomorphism if and only if $\Gamma$ primitively positively interprets all finite structures; in other words, this ability of $\Gamma$ is characterised by the absence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, a purely algebraic condition.sence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, i.e., a purely algebraic condition.
item.dc:creator: Leopold Karl, Michael Pinsker

item.title: The Ordering Principle and Higher Dependent Choice
item.description: arXiv:2510.14821v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide, for any regular uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, a new argument for Pincus' result on the consistency of $\mathrm{ZF}$ with the higher dependent choice principle $\mathrm{DC}_{<\kappa}$ and the ordering principle in the presence of a failure of the axiom of choice. We also generalise his methods and obtain these consistency results in a larger class of models.
item.dc:creator: Peter Holy, Jonathan Schilhan

item.title: A non-trivially non-trivial automorphism at an inaccessible cardinal
item.description: arXiv:2609.08061v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that, relative to the existence of an inaccessible cardinal, it is consistent that for an inaccessible cardinal $\kappa$, there is a non-trivial automorphism of $\mathcal{P}(\kappa)/\mathrm{fin}$ whose restriction to $\mathcal{P}(\beta)/\mathrm{fin}$ is induced by a bijection on $\beta$ for every $\beta<\kappa$. This answers questions posed by Larson--McKenney, Shelah--Stepr\=ans, and Veli\v{c}kovi\'{c}.
item.dc:creator: M\'{a}rk Po\'{o}r, Jing Zhang

item.title: Adding unbounded and not bounded sets to a singular cardinal
item.description: arXiv:2611.12848v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper solves a problem (SP) attributed to Solovay in the 1960s, which is to add an unbounded sequence to a singular cardinal $\kappa$ without adding bounded subsets to $\kappa$, while preserving $\kappa^+$. The solution applies to any cofinality of the singular cardinal, with the assumption that $\kappa$ is a strong limit needed for the case of uncountable cofinality. Unsuccessful attempts to solve (SP), mostly for the countable cofinality, have appeared in published papers by various authors.
item.dc:creator: Mirna D{\vz}amonja, Vladimir Kanovei

item.title: An Algebraic Abstraction of the Localic Sheafification via the Tripos-to-Topos Construction
item.description: arXiv:2511.06945v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Localic and realizability toposes are two central classes of toposes in categorical logic, both arising from the Hyland, Johnstone and Pitts tripos-to-topos construction. We investigate the common geometric structure underlying these classes by developing an algebraic abstraction of localic presheaves, localic sheafification, and the role of supercompactification in the Comparison Lemma. The resulting framework applies to a broad class of toposes arising from the tripos-to-topos construction, including all $\set$-based triposes. These results establish a common geometric framework encompassing both localic and realizability toposes.
item.dc:creator: Maria Emilia Maietti, Davide Trotta
